decisions.question: What lineage does the TopicRemoved error a forced removeTopic raises at a topology read carry (S65: neither bus-api@v2 nor topology-dsl@v2 says; topology-dsl lists the errors that carry none and TopicRemoved is not on it)?

options.label: none, recovered with Lineage.root()
options.consequence: As a timeout error: a catchError that recovers it gives a value whose publish has no causation, no parent correlations and a fresh correlation id, so it starts a new flow. Every causation id stays the id of a published envelope that caused the value (topic-model@v1 'How the lineage functions are applied'). topology-dsl's carry-none list needs a matching wording touch.

options.label: the lineage of the read's last delivered value
options.consequence: A recovered value continues the flow that last reached the topic and names that envelope as its cause, although no message caused the removal; undefined for a read that received nothing yet (an event topic, an unconnected read), which would need a fallback rule.

options.label: leave it unstated
options.consequence: The new case could not pin the recovered value's envelope; two runtimes could differ in what an observer or recorder sees after a recovered removal, and topology-dsl's first Errors and lineage sentence invites the second reading.

decisions.why: A removal is a shell operation, not a publish: no envelope causes it, so giving it a causation would put a false edge in the causation chain that Spec §2.4 'Correlation vs. Causation' and topic-model@v1 make walkable through published envelopes only. It is the same reason topology-dsl@v2 gives a timeout error none: the error is raised by an event that is not a value. The v2 stand-in already behaves this way (its catchError recovers an unwrapped error with Lineage.root()), and a seeded defect that gives the error the read's last lineage fails only the new case. The Specification is silent (Spec §3.2, §7.5 describe removeTopic without the error's lineage). What would have changed my mind: a Specification or Guide statement that a removal is traced as a message, or a consumer that needs to correlate a recovery with the flow that last touched the topic.
evidence: hsdd/contract/topology-dsl.md Errors and lineage (timeout and raw-operator errors carry none)
hsdd/contract/topic-model.md 'How the lineage functions are applied', G18

decisions.chosen: one read reaching two chains, under bus-api-v2

The orchestrator allowed either location; bus-api-v2 already holds the v2, v1 and minimal-barrier runtimes the replay needs, unchanged.

decisions.question: Classify the G9 clarification (a catchError on the path recovers TopicRemoved; it carries no lineage) against bus-api@v2's own Breaking list.

options.label: compatible, within v2
options.consequence: A dated 'Touched within v2' entry in ## Versioning; version, status and phase_ids unchanged; no consumer reference moves. Matches the Compatible item 'a new guarantee that existing fixtures still pass'.

options.label: breaking, bus-api@v3
options.consequence: A third version inside one intake for a rule no runtime or consumer behaves otherwise on; every consumer reference moves again (DEC-688).

decisions.why: No declaration changed. The recovery is not a new delivery rule: G22 already has activation interpret the plan as topology-dsl@v2's Live interpretation states, and its Errors and lineage rules (restated at S65 to name TopicRemoved) let a catchError recover any error, so a runtime that ended a recovered chain already broke topology-dsl@v2 G26 through G22. The lineage was unstated, as G41's off-type behavior was before v1 amendment (g), which this file classified compatible for the same reason. Every one of the 108 existing cases passes on the v2 runtime with the new case (109 of 109), and all three runtimes of the experiment, v1 included, pass the new case, so it reverses no fixture. bus-api@v2 is a draft authored in this intake with no package or consumer code (DEC-813). What would have changed my mind: an existing case, here or in a consumer's suite, that asserted a recovered removal still ended its chain.
